To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the partial substitution of Nacl by KCl, glycine or potassium lactate had little effect on microbial stability, but flavour and/or texturally defects were detected by panel analysis at levels above 20% of substitution by KCl or 30% by glycine.

the partial substitution of NaCL by KCL, potassium lactate or glycine had little effects on microbiological stability, but flavour and/or texturial defects were detected by the panelists with substitution levels above 40% for KCl, 20% for glycine and 30% for potassium lactate.
the partial replacement of NaCl by glycine, K-lactat or KCl had little effect on the microbiological stability but important sensory defects were detected with substitution levels above 30%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for reducing the NaCl in fermented sausage, and it is shown that the partial substitution by KCl and/or K-lactate can be a useful strategy to achieve this goal.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the partial replacement of NaCl by the different components evaluated in this research was not possible without affecting the sensory quality of the product.
the substitution of NaCl with KCl, KCl/gly, or K-lact/gly mixtures is not a viable strategy for the production of fermented meat products with reduced NaCl levels.
the replacement of NaCl in fermented sausages by other salts is not possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partial substitution of Nacl by KCl, glycine and K-Lactate in fermented sausage is possible but the levels of substitution should be limited to 40, 20 and 30% respectively.
the partial substitution of Nacl in fermented sausages is not recommended, because of the sensory defects detected.

the substitution of NaCl with the individual components KCl, KCl/glycin or K-lactate did not permit an important increase in the substitution levels compared to NaCl, because of important flavour and/or texturial defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the partial substitution of NaC by KCl, glycine and K lactate in fermented meat products does not affect the microbiological stability of the product but it does have a significant effect on the sensory characteristics of the product.
it is not possible to substitute NaCl with KCl, K-Lactate or glycine at levels higher than 30% without causing sensory defects.

the partial substitution of Nacl by KCl, glycine, K-lactates and their mixtures in fermented sausages has little effect on microbial stability, but the substitution levels should not exceed 40% with KCl and K-lactates, and 20% for glycine, to avoid sensory defects.
